c.tagline: Indonesia's City of Heroes - old harbor quarters, monuments, and the bridge to Madura.

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird is the reliable metered-taxi brand; insist on the meter, or use Gojek/Grab for fixed up-front pricing. App-booked motorbike taxis (ojek) are cheapest for beating traffic on short trips.

emergency.note: 112 is the nationwide emergency line; 113 reaches the fire service.

avoid.reason: Keep bags away from the roadside against motorbike snatch theft, and watch valuables in crowded markets like Pasar Turi and on city buses.

hood_desc: The commercial heart along historic Jalan Tunjungan, home to the colonial Hotel Majapahit, Tunjungan Plaza, and clusters of business hotels; the most central and convenient base for first-timers.
A leafy, well-connected central district around Gubeng railway station, full of cafes, eateries, and mid-range hotels; a handy transport hub popular with younger travelers.
An elegant colonial-era residential avenue (Jalan Raya Darmo) of villas, the Surabaya Zoo, and quiet tree-lined streets; a calm, upscale area to stay.

Surabaya's restored old town north of the center, taking in the Ampel Arab Quarter and Sunan Ampel Mosque, Chinatown around Kembang Jepun, the Red Bridge (Jembatan Merah), and the House of Sampoerna; the city's main heritage sightseeing zone.
The modern western suburbs built around the huge Pakuwon Mall and Ciputra World, with newer high-rise hotels and family attractions; a contemporary shopping-focused base.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water only.

transit.hours: Suroboyo Bus and Trans Semanggi buses run roughly 5:00 AM to around 10:00 PM; the KRL Commuterline and local trains run through the day. Ride-hailing fills late-night gaps.
transit.note: Surabaya's public transport is bus-based: the city-run Suroboyo Bus (famous for accepting recyclable plastic bottles as fare), the Trans Semanggi Suroboyo corridors, Trans Jatim regional buses, and Wirawiri Suroboyo feeder minibuses, plus traditional angkot (locally called bemo) and the KRL Commuterline / local trains linking Gubeng and Pasar Turi stations. Gojek and Grab are widely used.
transit.pay: The Suroboyo Bus can be paid with recyclable plastic bottles or a cashless card/app; Trans Semanggi and Trans Jatim use low flat cash/QRIS fares. Angkot fares are cash to the driver. Trains use tickets or the KRL card.

bus: Intercity buses from Purabaya (Bungurasih) and Tambak Osowilangun terminals
ferry: Ferries and Pelni ships from Tanjung Perak Port to Kalimantan, Sulawesi, and eastern Indonesia; Ujung-Kamal ferry toward Madura
train: KRL Commuterline and local trains (Gubeng, Pasar Turi)
Intercity trains to Jakarta, Yogyakarta, Malang, and Banyuwangi from Gubeng and Pasar Turi stations

transit.m: Damri airport bus to Bungurasih terminal and city points (~45-60 min)
Airport taxi to city center (30-45 min in traffic)

tip.r: Not expected; some restaurants add a service charge, and rounding up the bill for good service is appreciated but not required.

food.name: Rujak cingur
food.desc: Surabaya's defining dish: boiled cow's snout with vegetables, tofu, tempeh and fruit, bound in a thick black sauce of fermented shrimp paste and peanuts.

places.name: Rujak Cingur Ahmad Jais
places.note: The name locals give first; long queues at lunch and a properly pungent petis sauce.

places.name: Rujak Cingur Joko Dolog
places.note: Daytime warung beside the old statue park, open roughly 10am to 4pm.

places.name: Rujak Cingur Genteng Durasim
places.note: Old-town favourite in the market quarter, milder for first-timers.

food.name: Rawon
food.desc: Inky black beef soup coloured by keluak nuts - earthy and slightly sour - served with rice, bean sprouts, salted egg and a fierce sambal.

places.name: Rawon Setan Mbak Endang
places.note: Devil's rawon, so named for its old midnight hours; opposite the JW Marriott.

places.name: Rawon Kalkulator
places.note: Named for the cashier who totted up bills in her head; a Bungkul park institution.

places.name: Rawon Nguling
places.note: Surabaya outpost of the famous Probolinggo rawon house, richer and beefier.

food.name: Lontong balap
food.desc: Rice cakes with bean sprouts, fried tofu and crunchy lentho bean fritters in a light sweet-soy broth, topped with sambal petis and satay of cockles.

places.name: Lontong Balap Pak Gendut
places.note: Serving the dish since the late 1950s; the reference version in the city.

places.name: Lontong Balap Garuda Pak Gendut
places.note: The other long-running Pak Gendut stall, busiest at breakfast.

places.name: Lontong Balap Rajawali
places.note: Old-town stall in the colonial quarter, good early-morning stop.

food.name: Sate klopo
food.desc: Beef and fat skewers rolled in seasoned grated coconut before grilling, so the crust chars and sweetens; served with rice cakes and peanut sauce.

places.name: Sate Klopo Ondomohen Bu Asih
places.note: The original coconut-satay stall, open from early morning until late at night.

places.name: Satay stalls on Jalan Ondomohen
places.note: Neighbouring grills on the same street when Bu Asih's queue is long.

places.name: Pasar Atum food stalls
places.note: Market hall with satay counters and dozens of other Surabaya street classics.

food.name: Tahu tek and tahu campur
food.desc: Fried tofu snipped up with rice cake, egg and bean sprouts under a peanut-petis sauce; tahu campur is the beef-broth version with cassava fritters.

places.name: Tahu Campur Kalasan
places.note: The street that gave the dish its Surabaya name; stalls fire up in the evening.

places.name: Tahu Tek Pak Ali
places.note: Long-running night stall known for the loud snip of the scissors.

places.name: Evening warungs on Jalan Kalasan
places.note: A whole strip of tahu campur sellers competing side by side after dark.

food.name: Nasi cumi hitam
food.desc: Late-night plate of rice with squid cooked in its own ink, plus fried lung, tempeh and sambal - a Surabaya night-market speciality.

places.name: Nasi Cumi Pasar Atum
places.note: Pavement stall beside the market that opens late and runs into the early hours.

places.name: Pasar Atum food stalls
places.note: Indoor market alternative with squid, seafood and Chinese-Indonesian counters.

places.name: Night stalls on Jalan Kembang Jepun
places.note: The Kya-Kya strip in old Chinatown fills with seafood and rice stalls at night.

food.name: Es dawet and jus alpukat
food.desc: Iced coconut-milk and palm-sugar dawet with green rice-flour jelly, or thick avocado juice laced with chocolate syrup - the standard warung coolers.

places.name: Warungs on Jalan Kalasan
places.note: Juice and dawet carts sit alongside the tahu campur stalls.

places.name: Pasar Atum food stalls
places.note: Juice counters blend avocado, soursop and melon to order.

places.name: Taman Bungkul night stalls
places.note: Park-side drink carts busy every evening; good with rawon.

food.name: Es krim kuno Zangrandi
food.desc: Ice-cream sodas, floats and tutti-frutti sundaes from a 1930s Italian-founded parlour - Surabaya's most nostalgic cold drink.

places.name: Zangrandi Ice Cream
places.note: Open-air rattan chairs since the 1930s; the soda floats are the signature.

places.name: Zangrandi Manyar
places.note: Newer branch of the same parlour on the east side of the city.

places.name: Pasar Atum food stalls
places.note: Es campur and shaved-ice counters if you want the street version.

landmarks: Heroes Monument (Tugu Pahlawan)
A soaring 41-meter obelisk commemorating the 1945 Battle of Surabaya, the city's most recognizable patriotic landmark.
Suroboyo Statue (Patung Sura dan Buaya)
The famous shark-and-crocodile statue that gives Surabaya its name, a favorite photo spot symbolizing the city's origin legend.
Surabaya Submarine Monument (Monkasel)
A real decommissioned Soviet-era submarine beached on the riverbank and open for tours, a quirky and unmistakable city landmark.
House of Sampoerna
A beautifully preserved Dutch colonial-era clove cigarette factory and museum where visitors can watch traditional hand-rolling in action.
Gedung Negara Grahadi
An elegant 18th-century colonial mansion with grand pillars, now the East Java governor's office and a striking piece of Surabaya's heritage streetscape.
Al Akbar Mosque
Indonesia's second-largest mosque, distinguished by its turquoise domes and towering 99-meter minaret offering panoramic city views.
Jembatan Merah (Red Bridge)
A historic bridge in old Surabaya's Chinatown-adjacent trading district, site of fierce 1945 fighting and now a lively heritage quarter.
Surabaya Zoo (Kebun Binatang Surabaya)
One of Southeast Asia's oldest and largest zoos, a beloved city institution and green escape in the heart of Surabaya.
Jalan Tunjungan
Surabaya's historic main thoroughfare lined with Art Deco colonial-era buildings, capturing the city's early-20th-century commercial glory.
Balai Pemuda
A graceful Dutch colonial social hall turned cultural center, its neoclassical facade a favorite backdrop for photos in central Surabaya.

train.note: No international trains. Surabaya Gubeng is the main station for long-distance services, with Pasar Turi handling the northern coastal route; trains reach Jakarta in 9-11 hours, Yogyakarta in 4-5 and Malang in about 2. Book on the KAI Access app from 45 days out. For Mount Bromo, take the train or bus to Probolinggo and continue by jeep.

bus.note: No international coaches. Terminal Purabaya (Bungurasih) south of the city is one of Indonesia's busiest, with constant departures to Malang, Banyuwangi, Yogyakarta and through-services to Bali via the Ketapang-Gilimanuk ferry, around 12 hours. Book through redBus Indonesia (https://www.redbus.id/) or buy at the terminal.

intl.to: Kalimantan, Sulawesi, Nusa Tenggara & eastern Indonesia - sails from Tanjung Perak

intl.op: local ferry operators — tickets at Ujung terminal

ferry.note: No international sailings. Tanjung Perak is one of Indonesia's two great passenger ports, with Pelni ships heading east to Makassar, Flores, Maluku and Papua on voyages of several days - the cheapest way to reach the outer islands. The old Madura ferry still runs, though most traffic now uses the Suramadu bridge. Buy Pelni tickets at the port office or online well ahead of the holiday peaks.

half.name: Trowulan
half.blurb: Archaeological site of the former Majapahit empire capital, with brick temple ruins and a museum.

half.name: Malang
half.blurb: Cooler hill city known for Dutch colonial architecture and waterfalls in the surrounding highlands.

half.name: Madura Island
half.blurb: Island across the Suramadu Bridge known for traditional bull races and coastal salt farms.

full.name: Mount Bromo
full.blurb: Active volcano crater viewed at sunrise from a viewpoint across the surrounding Tengger caldera.
